newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatia says to offer concessions for free zones.
newsitem.headline: Croatia says to offer concessions for free zones.

text.p: Croatia's Economy Minister Davor Stern said on Thursday the government planned to offer concessions for companies to operate four free zones in bid to draw foreign investments.
"We'll soon issue a tender for Rijeka, Osijek, Sibenik and Krapina zones," Stern told an investment conference.
All four lie close to Croatia's borders, allowing good access for imported goods, he said and added that they would be operated according to a South Asian model.
"We are looking for a concessioner...it would operate the free zone and attract investors," Stern said.

Croatia passed a new law on free zones in May which it thought would be alluring to foreigners, eager to expand on its markets. But the interest so far has been limited to the sea port of Rijeka only.
Apart from these four, Stern said the government might consider further concessions for other free zones if the bidders offered good terms. -- Zoran Radosavljevic, Zagreb Newsroom, 385-1-4557075
